comentarios.texto: Adding members performs one `User` query per username, so bulk additions slow linearly with the count. Load all matching users in one query with `User.where(username: usernames.split(","))` before adding them to the group.

hist.text: groups_controller.rb:71-75 in the new add_members action calls User.find_by_username per username (N+1); this is an admin-only action with small inputs, so batching is a minor optimization.

The added add_members action loops over every supplied username and calls User.find_by_username separately (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-74); that method executes find_by(username_lower: ...) (app/models/user.rb:175-176). Consequently, large bulk additions incur one database lookup per username, creating avoidable database round trips and latency. Batching should preserve the existing case-insensitive lookup semantics.

Keep TP/nit, low. The N+1 is real in the new add_members (groups_controller.rb:71-75), but it is an admin-only action fed by a hand-typed comma-separated list, and the removed update_patch at base did the same per-username User.find_by_username loop, so the PR does not regress anything. group.add(user) still issues one write per user, so batching the lookup saves little. Minor performance with no user-visible effect = nit/low per the severity rubric.

The per-username query exists, but base update_patch already performed the same User.find_by_username and group.add loop. The new add_members action retains that lookup logic while changing the request format to comma-separated usernames, so the reported performance issue is pre-existing under the relocation ruling. I change my classification to FP; the minor admin-path optimization warrants low severity.
